q: What lock fits two bores at right angles, one through the door face and one through the edge?
n: Cylindrical (bored) locks install in two holes.

q: What adds a second layer of security to a main door lockset?
n: A deadbolt throws a separate solid bolt.

q: Which lockset suits interior doors that need no locking?
n: Passage sets latch but don't lock.

q: Which lockset combines a latch and a deadbolt in one unit?
n: Mortise locks house both in one case.

q: What hinge has one leaf mortised into the door edge and the other surface-mounted on the frame?
n: Half-mortise hinges are mortised on one side only.

q: Which of these doors does NOT hang on hinges?
n: Sliding doors run on tracks.

q: What hinge suits a door between kitchen and dining area that swings both ways?
n: Double-acting hinges let servers push through either way.

q: Which hinge runs the full length of the door and suits heavy, high-use doors?
n: It spreads the load along the whole edge.

q: Which hinge closes the door by its own built-in spring?
n: Spring hinges self-close.

q: Which door is commonly used for wardrobes?
n: Bifolds open wide in shallow space.

q: Which of these is a door leaf material?
n: Plywood skins flush doors.

q: What is the structural member placed over a door or window opening?
n: A header (lintel) carries the load above the opening.

q: Which door type saves the most space?
n: Sliding doors need no swing clearance.

q: Which of these is a well-known lockset brand in the Philippines?
n: Davies is paint and HCG is sanitary ware.

q: Which brand is widely used locally for high-security locksets and deadbolts?
n: Davies and Nippon are paint brands.

q: Which brand is popular for door closers and floor hinges?
n: Dorma (dormakaba) specializes in closers and floor springs.

q: Which brand is known for premium architectural hinges and sliding door systems?
n: Häfele is a furniture and architectural hardware maker.

q: What hardware goes on a fire exit door?
n: Panic hardware opens by push in an emergency.

q: Which door type best keeps outside air from entering a building?
n: A revolving door is never open straight through.

q: What must be known when ordering door jambs?
n: The jamb depth matches the wall thickness.

q: What sets the height of a door jamb?
n: The jamb is sized to the door leaf.

q: What sets the clear width between door jambs?
n: The jambs frame the leaf's width.

q: What is the purpose of a threshold under a door?
o: A seal against air, water, dust and sound
n: Thresholds seal the gap and mark the change in floor finish.

q: Which way must an emergency exit door swing?
o: Outward, in the direction of egress
n: Exit doors swing with the direction of travel.

q: Which exit door construction gives the best fire resistance?
n: Rated steel assemblies hold the longest.

q: What kind of closer is required on fire-rated exit doors?
n: Fire doors must be self-closing.

q: What is added at the bottom of a fire exit door to stop smoke?
n: Smoke seals close the gap at the floor.

q: What makes a pair of fire exit doors close in the correct order?
n: The coordinator holds the active leaf until the inactive leaf closes.

q: Which window keeps rain out while still letting air in during a downpour?
n: The top-hinged sash acts as a hood.

q: Which window is hardest to reach?
n: Clerestories sit high on the wall.

q: Which window is common in shower areas?
n: Small high awnings vent and shed water.

q: Which window gives the best natural ventilation?
n: A casement opens its full area and scoops breeze.

q: Which window should NOT open onto a hallway?
n: An outward sash swings into the walkway.

q: What is a long horizontal band of windows called?
n: Ribbon windows run in a continuous strip.

q: A high-rise condo uses mostly fixed windows with small openings for safety. What does this give up?
n: Fixed glazing still gives a view but little airflow.

q: What fills the space between the panes of double-glazed windows?
n: The sealed gap holds dry air or argon.

q: What is the proper way to install a steel window frame?
o: Either way, depending on the installer
Finish the opening first, then set the frame
Set the frame before finishing the opening
n: Steel frames are set and grouted, then the opening is finished around them.

q: Which window is hinged at the top?
n: Awnings swing out from the top.

q: Which window is hinged at the side?
n: Casements swing like doors.

q: Which window has adjustable horizontal glass slats?
n: Jalousie blades pivot together.

q: Which window runs on a horizontal track and doesn't project in or out?
n: Sliders stay in the wall plane.

q: Which window is fixed and cannot open?
n: Picture windows are fixed glazing.

q: What is the main disadvantage of wooden windows?
o: They shrink and swell with the weather
n: Moisture movement causes sticking and gaps.

q: Which window looks cheaper because it uses ordinary hinges?
n: Wood casements hang on plain butt hinges.

q: Which window is most likely to leak air without maintenance?
n: Overlapping blades never seal tightly.
